aio-passage.pageDescription: Research shows AIs preferentially cite 134-167 word self-contained passages. Paste a draft OR analyze a live URL — we split it into chunks, score each on length, self-containment, Q→A structure, factual concreteness, and source citation.
aio-passage.noPassages: Couldn't extract any passages — make sure paragraphs are separated by blank lines.
aio-passage.noRewrite: AI didn't return a rewrite. Either the passage already scores 70+ or no AI provider is configured.
aio-passage.invalidUrl: That doesn't look like a valid URL.
aio-passage.fetchFailed: Couldn't fetch or parse that URL.
aio-passage.noPassagesUrl: Fetched the page but couldn't split it into scoreable passages. The main content may be too short or too fragmented.
aio-passage.markdownPlaceholder: Paste your blog post markdown here…
aio-passage.pasteHint: Deterministic scoring — no AI cost. AI rewrite hints are optional per passage.
aio-passage.urlHint: Fetches the URL server-side, strips chrome, and scores each paragraph. Works on any public HTML page.
aio-passage.lowScorers: {count, plural, one {# passage} other {# passages}} below the 70 threshold. Batch-rewrite all of them in parallel to get a full before/after report.

cannibalization.pageDescription: Find queries where 2+ pages on your site compete for the same ranking — Google can't decide which to surface, both suffer. Pulls 28 days of GSC query+page data and groups by query.
cannibalization.setupTitle: Connect Google Search Console to use this
cannibalization.setupDetail: Finding pages that compete with each other needs the queries each one actually ranks for, which only Search Console has.
cannibalization.filterHint: Only flags queries where ≥2 pages each pull ≥5 impressions and at least one is in the top 30 — filters out random long-tail noise.
cannibalization.noneDetected: No cannibalization detected in the last 28 days.
cannibalization.groupsHint: Expand a row to see the competing pages. Recommended keeper is the page with the best current position — usually the one Google is already favoring. Fix: canonical or 301 the rest to it, or differentiate their intent.

canonical-audit.pageDescription: Crawl a site, flag every page where rel=canonical points somewhere broken: missing entirely, multiple tags, off-host, broken target, redirect target, self-mismatch (different trailing slash / scheme / casing), or noindex+canonical conflict. Catches the silent SEO bug that kills indexation.
canonical-audit.findingBrokenTarget: Canonicals pointing at a URL that does not load
canonical-audit.findingSelfMismatch: Canonicals that disagree with the page's own URL
canonical-audit.findingMultiple: Pages with more than one canonical tag
canonical-audit.noIssues: No canonical issues detected on the first {count} pages.

cluster.pageDescription: Type a head topic → we mine PAA + related searches + autocomplete + Reddit. AI assembles a hub-and-spoke architecture: 1 pillar + 15-20 spokes with slugs, intent, format, and an internal-linking map. The 1-day strategy plan, in 60 seconds.

crux.pageDescription: Real Chrome user data for this URL over the last 28 days. Unlike Lighthouse / PageSpeed (lab numbers), this is what actual users experienced. Note Google assesses Core Web Vitals at origin level — use the CrUX Origin Summary to see where you actually stand.
crux.originFallbackHint: Falls back to origin-level data when the URL itself doesn't have enough traffic.
crux.noData: No CrUX data available — this URL/origin has too little Chrome traffic over the last 28 days. Try a more popular page or use the <link>synthetic PageSpeed scan</link> instead.
crux.historyTitle: Trend over the last six months
crux.historyIntro: CrUX History: one 28-day window per week. Neighbouring windows share three weeks, so the latest is compared with the window four weeks earlier — the nearest one with no days in common.
crux.noHistory: No CrUX history for this URL or its origin — too little Chrome traffic.
crux.notEnoughLatest: Not enough data in the latest window.
crux.noEarlierWindow: No window four weeks earlier to compare with.
crux.regressed: More than 20% worse than four weeks earlier.

hreflang.pageDescription: Checks every hreflang tag (in HTML + HTTP Link header), validates format + self-reference + x-default, then verifies reciprocal links on each variant.
hreflang.invalidFormat: Invalid hreflang format. Use lang or lang-region (e.g. en, en-US).
hreflang.issueNoTags: No hreflang tags found. If this site has language/region variants, add them.
hreflang.issueNoXDefault: Missing x-default. Recommended as the fallback for unmatched locales.
hreflang.issueNoSelfReference: Page doesn't include a self-referencing hreflang. Each variant should reference itself.
hreflang.issueDuplicateLang: Multiple hrefs for "{lang}". Each language should point to one URL.
hreflang.issueNotReciprocal: {url} doesn't point back at this URL. Reciprocal links are required for hreflang.
hreflang.findingNoXDefaultTitle: No x-default set for unmatched locales
hreflang.findingNoXDefaultDetails: x-default is what Google falls back to for a visitor whose language matches none of the versions listed. Without it, that choice is made for you.
hreflang.findingNotReciprocalTitle: {count, plural, one {# alternate does not link back} other {# alternates do not link back}}
hreflang.findingNotReciprocalDetails: Hreflang has to be mutual. Google ignores a set whose members disagree, so these alternates currently do nothing: {urls}
hreflang.findingUnreachableTitle: {count, plural, one {# alternate URL could not be fetched} other {# alternate URLs could not be fetched}}
hreflang.findingUnreachableDetails: An alternate that does not load cannot be indexed, so the visitors it was meant for land on the wrong version: {urls}
hreflang.reciprocalHint: Each variant should reference back to this URL. Up to 6 of the most common variants checked.

hreflang-gen.pageDescription: Paste a list of language-region pairs and URLs. We emit the full hreflang block (HTML + HTTP-header + sitemap formats) with x-default validation. Avoids the silent self-reference bug that breaks 60% of hand-written hreflang implementations.
hreflang-gen.warnNoXDefault: Missing x-default. Strongly recommended for any multi-language setup.
hreflang-gen.pairsLabel: Language / region tab URL — one TAB-separated pair per line. Include x-default.

keyword-difficulty.pageDescription: Heuristic difficulty score (0-100) computed from real SERP signals — no Ahrefs / Semrush key needed. Combines big-brand presence in top 10, SERP-feature occupation, title competitiveness, and your AI key (if configured) for a plain-language take on how to compete.
keyword-difficulty.serpFailed: SERP scrape failed — try again in a minute.
keyword-difficulty.serpEmpty: Couldn't read SERP results. Try a different query.
keyword-difficulty.hint: Scrapes the live SERP via headless browser. First run can take ~10s.
keyword-difficulty.whyTitle: Why we scored it that way
keyword-difficulty.bigBrandsHard: Wikipedia / Reddit / Forbes etc — hard to outrank
keyword-difficulty.featuredSnippetHint: Win-win-back if you can answer better

link-checker.pageDescription: Paste any URL — we extract every '<'a'>' link, classify internal vs external, dofollow vs nofollow, and surface the most-used anchor texts. Critical for outbound link audits before publishing.
link-checker.fetchFailed: Couldn't fetch — site unreachable or timeout.
link-checker.topAnchorsHint: Heavy repetition of one anchor text is a keyword-stuffing smell — vary your anchors.

link-graph.pageDescription: Crawls the site, builds a link graph, and surfaces orphan pages with AI-free content-similarity-based suggestions for where to link them from. Free, fast, no LLM required.
link-graph.orphansHint: For each, the top-3 most-relevant source pages (by TF-IDF cosine similarity). Add a contextual link from one of them.
link-graph.hubsHint: Pages with 5+ inbound internal links. They're your authority distributors — make sure they link to your most-important pages.

meta-tag-generator.pageDescription: Produces 3 SEO-optimized title + description options for any page — keyword-led, benefit-led, and curiosity-led angles. Copy-paste ready HTML. Also generates Open Graph tags for social shares.
meta-tag-generator.aiNotConfigured: AI provider not configured. Add an API key in Settings → AI.
meta-tag-generator.parseFailed: Couldn't parse AI response — try again.
meta-tag-generator.noOptions: AI returned no options. Try again.
meta-tag-generator.topicLabel: Page topic (1-2 sentences about the page)
meta-tag-generator.topicPlaceholder: A landing page for our small-business invoicing app. Covers free plan, recurring invoices, payment reminders.
meta-tag-generator.optionsTitle: 3 options — pick the angle that fits your page

migration-parity.pageDescription: Paste your pre-migration URL list. We hit each one, follow redirects, surface what's broken / unredirected / drifted off-host. Run pre-launch and post-launch — the diff is your migration QA.
migration-parity.newDomainPlaceholder: new domain (optional, e.g. newsite.com — used to flag redirects that drift off-host)

news-headline.pageDescription: Score a journalistic headline. Length, Top Stories fit (30-110 chars sweet spot), AP-style hook, primary keyword placement. AI suggests 3-5 alternates.
news-headline.headlinePlaceholder: Senate passes infrastructure bill in 67-32 vote

outreach-personalize.pageDescription: Paste a prospect URL + your generic template. AI fetches their site, finds their recent posts and topical signals, and rewrites your opener with one specific reference. Turns a 2% reply rate into 15%.
outreach-personalize.goalPlaceholder: Pitch a guest post / link insertion / partnership
outreach-personalize.templatePlaceholder:
Hi there,

I write about [topic] over at [site]. Wanted to share a piece I think your readers would like — [link]. Mind if I send the highlights?

Thanks,
[name]
outreach-personalize.subject: Subject

pagerank.pageDescription: Crawls your site, builds the link graph, runs 30 iterations of PageRank with damping=0.85. Surfaces your authority pages (hubs) and starved pages (low PR + few inbound links). The fastest way to find pages worth linking to that aren't currently being linked from anywhere.
pagerank.hubsNote: Pages with the highest computed PageRank — these power the rest of your site.
pagerank.starvedNote: Bottom-PR pages with ≤1 inbound link. Add internal links to these from your hubs.

rank-where.pageDescription: Enter a domain + keyword + country, get your exact position in Google's top 100. See who outranks you, whether AI Overview is present, and get specific fixes to climb.
rank-where.serpFailed: Couldn't fetch SERP. Try again in a minute.
rank-where.recoNotFound: Not in top {topN} for "{query}" in {country}. Start with content audit: do you have a page targeting this query at all?
rank-where.recoLandingPage: Build a dedicated landing page for this query — the Writing studio (/content) can draft it from the SERP.
rank-where.recoEntrenched: The SERP has Wikipedia/Reddit/YouTube in top 3 — entrenched. You'll likely never beat them; instead target long-tail variants or capture Reddit/YouTube real estate directly.
rank-where.recoBeyondPage1: Currently at #{position}. You're on page {page} — needs major work to crack page 1.
rank-where.recoGeoScore: Run the GEO composite score (/tools/geo-score) on the ranking page to find the weakest dimension.
rank-where.recoAioPassage: Run the AIO passage optimizer (/tools/aio-passage) — if AI Overview is present, the cited result usually outranks others.
rank-where.recoStriking: Solid position #{position} — striking distance. Refresh the page's content, add more E-E-A-T signals, target the 134-167 word AIO passages.
rank-where.recoRefresh: Use the /tools/refresh detector to find specific gaps vs the top 3 ranking pages.
rank-where.recoTop3: Already at #{position}. Maintain — focus on freshness (update content quarterly) and earn 1-2 new authoritative backlinks.
rank-where.recoAioNotCited: AI Overview triggers for this query but you're NOT cited. Add Article + Person schema, build 134-167 word self-contained answer passages.
rank-where.recoSnippetOnly: Featured snippet is yours but you don't show in classic top 10 — Google may be using a different page. Audit which URL holds the snippet.
rank-where.hint: Uses the shared headless-browser pool with stealth + proxy rotation. One scan per minute is fine; rapid repeats may trip Google's rate limiter.

refresh.pageDescription: Compare your published page to the current top-10 SERP. Surfaces missing topics, missing sections, and a concrete refresh plan you can hand to a writer or do yourself.
refresh.running: Diffing your page vs the SERP… (1-2 min)

render.pageDescription: Render any URL in headless Chrome (post-hydration HTML, full screenshot, redirect chain, response headers, console errors). Critical for SPAs / JS-heavy sites where a curl-style fetch shows you nothing.
render.noIssues: No console / network issues during page load.
